questions.question: Which gas makes up the largest fraction of Earth's dry atmosphere?
choices: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Argon

questions.question: What is atmospheric pressure primarily caused by?
choices: The temperature of air alone, regardless of its amount
Only the pressure exerted by falling rain
The weight of overlying air
The mass of water vapor without the other gases

questions.question: Which gas makes up about one-fifth of Earth's dry atmosphere?
choices: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Argon

questions.question: In which atmospheric layer does most weather occur?
choices: Troposphere
Stratosphere
Mesosphere
Thermosphere

questions.question: Which atmospheric layer contains most of the ozone layer?
choices: Troposphere
Mesosphere
Stratosphere
Exosphere

questions.question: What is a pressure gradient?
choices: A change in temperature over distance only
A change in pressure over distance
The pressure recorded at one point with no comparison
The humidity recorded over one hour

questions.question: What does humidity describe?
choices: Only liquid droplets suspended in clouds
Only the pressure of the atmosphere
The concentration of airborne dust
Water vapor in the air

questions.question: Why does air pressure generally decrease with altitude?
choices: The mass of each air molecule decreases with elevation
Gravity becomes stronger enough to remove pressure
There is less overlying air
High-altitude air contains no molecules

questions.question: Why can warmed air rise in surrounding cooler air?
choices: Warming increases density under the same outside pressure
Warm air rises because its particles lose all mass
Temperature differences have no effect on air density
It expands and becomes less dense under suitable conditions

questions.question: What drives horizontal air motion from pressure differences?
choices: The transfer of heat without a pressure difference
A pressure-gradient force
Only the attraction of air toward mountains
The weight of clouds as a separate horizontal force

questions.question: How does Earth's rotation affect large-scale moving air?
choices: It deflects its path through the Coriolis effect
It removes all pressure gradients
It forces all winds to travel vertically
It makes global air motion independent of pressure differences

questions.question: Why can rising moist air form clouds?
choices: Water vapor remains gaseous at every temperature
Expansion warms air enough to form liquid droplets
Expansion cools the air, allowing water vapor to condense
Rising air always loses all its water vapor

questions.question: Why do high-pressure systems often bring clearer weather?
choices: Descending air tends to warm and inhibit cloud formation
High pressure guarantees heavy rain everywhere
Descending air always cools by expansion
Clouds can form only when pressure is high

questions.question: Why is the ozone layer important?
choices: It blocks all visible sunlight from the surface
It supplies most atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis
It determines all surface wind directions
It absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation

questions.question: Why does air exert pressure on all sides of an object?
choices: Pressure acts only downward on exposed surfaces
Moving gas molecules collide with surfaces in many directions
Air molecules move in only one direction
Pressure exists only in sealed containers

questions.question: A climber measures lower pressure on a mountain than at sea level. Which explanation best fits?
choices: The mountain creates new gas molecules
Less air lies above the higher location
The sea-level air has no weight
Higher altitude always means stronger gravity

questions.question: Two nearby areas differ in pressure. Ignoring rotation and friction, which way is air accelerated?
choices: From lower toward higher pressure
Parallel to equal-pressure lines with no acceleration
Only toward warmer ground regardless of pressure
From higher toward lower pressure

questions.question: Warm air over land rises while cooler sea air moves inland at the surface. What circulation is described?
choices: A daytime sea breeze
A nighttime land breeze
A jet stream above the poles
An ocean tide

questions.question: A sealed flexible balloon expands as outside pressure decreases, with temperature unchanged. What explains the expansion?
choices: Its gas mass must increase immediately
Its temperature must rise despite the stated condition
The gas can occupy more volume under lower external pressure
Its internal pressure can never respond to external pressure

questions.question: Two air samples have the same temperature and volume, but one contains more gas particles. Which generally has greater pressure?
choices: The sample with fewer particles
Both must have zero pressure
The darker-colored sample
The sample with more particles
